title: FIRST PROPERTY TAX PAYMENT DUE TODAY
full_story:
The first installment of the 2025 payable 2026 Real Estate Tax Bill is due today.  Office hours today are from 8:00 am to 4:00pm.  If you have questions about your tax bill, please feel free to call the Treasurer’s office.  If you cannot get through, please leave a message, and they will return your call as soon as possible.  Phone 618-665-3727.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.

At the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money order.  Bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00-4:00 Monday through Friday but closed on national holidays.

Online by credit/debit card: Go to www.govpaynow.com PLC #a00082.

Or by drop box at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

title: HEALTH CARE VIOLATION
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH) has issued a $14,700 fine to Chestnut Corner, a shelter care facility in Louisville, following the release of its second-quarter report on nursing home violations.

The facility, located on West Chestnut Street in Louisville, was cited for widespread poor maintenance.  According to IDPH officials, inspectors utilized interviews, direct observations, and record reviews to determine that the facility failed to keep its interior finishes, furniture, plumbing, grounds, and electrical systems in good repair.  State officials warned that these systemic issues have the potential to impact all 73 residents living at the facility.

Specific deficiencies detailed in the state report include; water leaking from a basement ceiling in one of the buildings, overflowing trash containers, structural concerns, including walls bowing outward, missing tiles in the resident dining area, and mold growth in multiple shower areas.

title: COX SCHOLARSHIPS
full_story:
Frontier Community College announced that the Clemence Elizabeth Cox Nursing Scholarship, established by Jerry Cox in honor of his mother, has just awarded its 114th scholarship.

The funding helps alleviate financial barriers for students across the region during the 2026-2027 academic year.  In fact, the impact is already being felt locally, three of this year’s recipients have already secured employment with Fairfield Memorial Hospital to help address critical area workforce needs.

This year’s Clemence Elizabeth Cox Nursing Scholarship recipients are Allaryn Brach of Cisne, Megan Blazier of Norris City, Kadence Smith of Xenia, Talisa Church of Fairfield, and Morgan Chapman of Fairfield.

Additionally, the 2026-2027 Debra Jean Withrow Nursing Scholarship recipients are Talisa Church of Fairfield and Cindy Jolley of Geff.

Frontier Community College extends its sincere appreciation to Jerry Cox for his continued generosity and unwavering support of local nursing education.

Photo Caption: Front row, from left: Allaryn Brach, Megan Blazier, Jerry Cox, and Kadence Smith. Middle row: Julie Bullard, Allied Health Program Advisor; Talisa Church; Morgan Chapman; and Brianna Trowbridge, Nursing Faculty Instructor. Back row: Dr. Sharmila Kakac, FCC President; Nathan Gentz, Fairfield Memorial Hospital Foundation Director; David Savage, FCC Foundation; and Brittany Rose, Nursing Faculty Instructor. Not pictured: Cindy Jolley.

title: HAUNTED THEATER
full_story:
Nostalgia Theater presents Demented Holidays on Friday, October 23rd and Saturday, October 24th, from 7 to 11 pm each night.  This will be a walk-through haunted house.  Nostalgia Theater is located in downtown Flora in the former Town Theater building.

This year’s haunted house experience is even better than last year.  The thrills start with a pitch-dark haunted maze, a tour through terror-filled holidays, and a trip through the basement horrors.  Two stories of haunts await those that dare.

Ticket price is $10 per person and all tickets will be sold at the door.  This event may not be suitable for young children.

Money raised will be used for the continuing restoration of Nostalgia Theater.

title: ILLINOIS BASIN CELEBRATION
full_story:
The Illinois Basin Celebration is making its return to Oblong next month, bringing together local oil industry professionals for a day of networking, education, and community outreach.

Organizers say all regional oil industry professionals are invited to the event on November 4th, which kicks off in the morning with complimentary coffee and donuts, followed by a catered lunch.  Attendees will also walk away with free “IllinoisBasinProud” swag, including stocking caps and coffee tumblers.

This year’s core focus centers strictly on workplace safety.  Starting at 8:30 am, industry workers can attend non-mandatory, hour-long safety workshops.  Mark Weiler will host a session on general oilfield safety, while Illinois Eastern Community Colleges instructor Wes Taylor will lead training on H2S and CPR.

The celebration is also opening its doors to the next generation.  The Illinois Petroleum Resources Board will host museum tours and “Petro Pros” educational presentations.  Twenty-five students from Oblong Junior High School will visit on November 4th, followed by 23 students from Hutsonville High School and Newton St. Thomas Grade School on November 5th.

Local operators and industry professionals who want to participate in the school presentations or bring out oilfield equipment to show the students are highly encouraged to get involved.

If you plan to attend the lunch, organizers ask that you message them or reply to their announcement email to reserve your seat.  More than 40 professionals have already RSVP’d, and everyone who signs up ahead of time will be entered into a drawing for a 250-dollar gift card.

title: TROUT FISHING OPENS
full_story:
The 2026 Illinois fall trout fishing season will open tomorrow at 60 ponds, lakes and streams throughout the state.

In our area trout fishing can be done at the Sam Dale Conservation Area Turkey Run Pond in Wayne County.  At the Boston Pond, in the Stephen A. Forbes State Recreation Area in Marion County, and at the Mount Vernon City Park Pond in Jefferson County.

The Illinois Catchable Trout Program is funded through the sale of inland trout stamps.  The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) stocks more than 80,000 rainbow trout each year at waters where trout fishing is permitted during the fall season.  An additional 80,000 trout are stocked for the spring season, which begins in April.

For the 2026 fall trout season, no trout may be taken from any stocked site before the season opens.  During the season, the daily catch limit is five trout.  All anglers must have a valid Illinois fishing license and inland trout stamp.  Check the IDNR agent locator website for locations. Fishing licenses and trout stamps are also available online.

Anglers should contact individual trout-stocked sites for information about site-specific regulations and opening times.  Not all sites open at 5 am on opening day.  Anglers are encouraged to check the opening time for their preferred fishing location before Saturday.

The fall trout season offers opportunities for families to get outdoors and enjoy fishing.  Resources are available for taking kids fishing online.  For more information on trout seasons and other Illinois fishing opportunities, visit www.ifishillinois.org.

title: DEER ON THE MOVE
full_story:
Autumn in Illinois offers some of the most beautiful scenery anywhere in the country, with spectacular foliage, magical sunsets and stunning drives.  The Illinois Department of Transportation and Illinois Department of Natural Resources are reminding the public to anticipate seeing more deer on the roads as well, with peak mating season lasting through December.

“Deer are on the move throughout the state, increasing your chances of encountering one at any time,” said Illinois Transportation Secretary Gia Biagi.  “Stay alert, even during routine trips and your daily commute.  Following a few simple recommendations and rules can help you avoid a trip to the body shop – or worse.”

In 2025, there were 14,529 crashes involving deer in Illinois.  Of those, 13,846 resulted in damage to property or vehicles, while 677 caused injuries.  Six of the crashes resulted in seven fatalities.

Although a collision with deer can happen any time, Illinois is approaching the time of year when most occur.  Last year, 41% of crashes involving deer in Illinois occurred in October, November and December, with November being the highest-risk month.  Rural areas were the site of 69% of crashes involving deer.  Eight out of 10 collisions were at twilight or nighttime.

“Deer are plentiful across Illinois, and drivers should be aware of their presence,” said IDNR Director Jim Montgomery.  “Please be cautious while driving, as deer are notably active during fall mating season and around dawn and dusk.”

If you hit a deer, pull off to the shoulder, turn on your hazard lights and call 911.  Do not exit the vehicle to check on an injured deer or pull it from the road.

For information on how to claim a deer involved in a crash, or to report possession of a deer killed in a crash, visit the IDNR website at dnr.illinois.gov.

title: RURAL DEVELOPMENT GRANT APPLICATIONS
full_story:
The Illinois Farm Bureau Rural Development Grant Program is now returning for its fourth year.  The application period is now open.

Last year, Illinois Farm Bureau awarded grants to 30 recipients.  For the 2026-27 grant cycle, $120,000 will be available to support rural development projects benefiting Illinois farmers, families and their communities.

“Rural communities know what they need to thrive, and our Rural Development Grant Program is one way Illinois Farm Bureau can help turn those local ideas into action,” said Ryan Tate, IFB associate director of local government.  “These grants support projects that strengthen economic opportunity, improve quality of life and address critical needs in rural communities.”

Multiple grants will be awarded, with past amounts ranging from $1,300 to $10,000.  Tate told FarmWeek IFB is excited to work with county Farm Bureaus and their local partners “to invest in the next set of projects that can make a lasting difference.”

Grants are available to groups and organizations including county Farm Bureaus, units of local government, economic development organizations, nonprofits, community groups and small businesses.  Tate said greater emphasis will be placed on projects ready to move forward and encouraged applicants whose projects are more than a year from being “ready to go” to consider applying in a future grant cycle.

COUNTRY Financial is once again contributing $20,000 of the $120,000 available through the program.  Sarah Franzen, COUNTRY senior corporate social responsibility specialist, said the company has long supported IFB’s “community-facing programs” and chose to support the Rural Development Grant Program because it brings communities together “to support projects that make a meaningful, lasting impact.”

“Thriving communities are built through partnership and shared purpose,” Franzen said.  “Together, we are helping create opportunities that strengthen rural Illinois and enrich the lives of those who call it home.”

Applications are due by December 1st.  Those interested in applying for a 2026-27 grant are encouraged to contact their county Farm Bureau to discuss their project and obtain an application link.

IFB expects applicants to be notified by February 28th.  For more information on the program, including the FAQs and the types of eligible projects, visit bit.ly/IFBrdgrants.
